LLY-2026-10-02: When did the FDA approve Jaypirca for first-line CLL?

The FDA approved pirtobrutinib (Jaypirca, Eli Lilly and Company) on October 2, 2026 for adult patients with previously untreated chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) or small lymphocytic lymphoma (SLL) with no known 17p deletion, per the FDA's approval notification of that date.

The FDA first approved Jaypirca on January 27, 2023, under accelerated approval for relapsed or refractory mantle cell lymphoma after at least two lines of systemic therapy including a BTK inhibitor. It added CLL/SLL after at least two prior lines of therapy including a BTK inhibitor and a BCL-2 inhibitor on December 1, 2023 (accelerated approval), granted traditional approval for adults with relapsed or refractory CLL/SLL previously treated with a covalent BTK inhibitor on December 3, 2025, and approved first-line use in CLL/SLL with no known 17p deletion on October 2, 2026.
What trial supported the Jaypirca first-line CLL approval?

BRUIN CLL-313 (NCT05023980), a randomized, open-label, active-controlled trial in 282 patients with previously untreated CLL or SLL without deletion of chromosome 17p, comparing pirtobrutinib with bendamustine plus a rituximab product. Progression-free survival assessed by an independent review committee had a hazard ratio of 0.20 (95% CI 0.11 to 0.37; p<0.0001), per the FDA.
What is the approved Jaypirca dose for CLL?

The FDA's notification gives the recommended pirtobrutinib dose as 200 mg orally once daily until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity. The FDA says full prescribing information will be posted on Drugs@FDA; Lilly's announcement links the current prescribing information.
RHHBY-2026-10-08: When did the FDA approve Tecentriq for Stage III colon cancer?

The FDA approved atezolizumab (Tecentriq, Genentech) on October 8, 2026, in combination with a fluoropyrimidine and oxaliplatin, for the adjuvant treatment of adult and pediatric patients two years of age and older with Stage III mismatch repair deficient (dMMR) colon cancer, per the FDA's approval notification of that date. Genentech had given October 9, 2026 as the goal date, so the action came one day early.
What trial supported the Tecentriq colon cancer approval?

ATOMIC/ML39057 (NCT02912559), a randomized, open-label, active-controlled trial in 711 adults and one pediatric patient with resected Stage III dMMR colon cancer, comparing atezolizumab plus mFOLFOX6 then atezolizumab alone with mFOLFOX6 alone. The disease-free survival hazard ratio was 0.50 (95% CI 0.35 to 0.73; p 0.0001), per the FDA.
Was Tecentriq Hybreza also approved for colon cancer?

Yes. The same FDA notification approved atezolizumab and hyaluronidase-tqjs (Tecentriq Hybreza) with a fluoropyrimidine and oxaliplatin for the adjuvant treatment of patients 12 years and older who weigh 40 kg or more with Stage III dMMR colon cancer.
What is the recommended Tecentriq dose for Stage III colon cancer?

For adults the FDA gives 840 mg every two weeks, 1200 mg every three weeks or 1680 mg every four weeks intravenously with chemotherapy for six months, then atezolizumab alone for six months or until disease recurrence or unacceptable toxicity. The FDA says full prescribing information will be posted on Drugs@FDA.
NVS-2026-10-06: When did the FDA approve Rhapsido for symptomatic dermographism?

The FDA's Drugs@FDA data record the approval of the Rhapsido (remibrutinib) efficacy supplement, NDA 218436 supplement 1, on October 6, 2026. Novartis announced it on October 7, 2026, for adults with symptomatic dermographism inadequately controlled by H1 antihistamines.
What trial supported the Rhapsido symptomatic dermographism approval?
The symptomatic dermographism cohort of the Phase III RemIND trial. Per Novartis, 29.3% of patients on Rhapsido achieved a complete response from hives at Week 12 versus 14.0% on placebo (p=0.0229).
The FDA first approved Rhapsido (remibrutinib) on September 30, 2025, for adults with chronic spontaneous urticaria inadequately controlled by H1 antihistamines (NDA 218436).
